correctness.rationale: Under a once-sampled Bernoulli shortcut and two fixed boundary agents, expected gossip converges (in expectation) to a grounded weighted-harmonic solution. Series/parallel effective resistance gives a(t)=(L/H+Lt)/(1+2L/H+2Lt), and linearity of the rest of the path follows from harmonicity. Direct subtraction yields the strictly positive rational Jensen gap. Summing the absolute coordinatewise differences on both short arms and the H+1 central vertices, avoiding double counting endpoints, yields the exact parity-dependent B_H coefficient. When H/L->infinity, p->0, Lp->c including infinity, normalized discrepancy tends to phi(c)/2, and convergence in probability holds because the realized shortcut is absent with probability 1-p->1. Independently solved 175 exact rational grounded Laplacian systems across lengths and shortcut conductances, plus 35 exact discrepancy checks. No assertion of almost-sure convergence of instantaneous gossip states is made.
residual_risks: The critical limit is conditional/graph-averaged expected opinion, not pathwise fluctuating gossip trajectory or arbitrary random graph. H/L->infinity and p->0 are essential.

originality.rationale: Acemoğlu–Como–Fagnani–Ozdaglar established the harmonic representation of stubborn-agent expected gossip, so the electric-network method is established. Xing–Johansson concentration bounds compare random-graph gossip to expected-graph averages under substantial graph density/anchoring hypotheses not met by the long low-degree path with one rare bridge. The sharp scale p~1/L, exact all-vertex discrepancy and supercritical limit 1/4 within this family are not consequences of their concentration statement. The theorem is a motivated sharp counterexample delineating the hypotheses, not claiming to refute those results.
residual_risks: Prior graph-electric-network rare-edge approximation counterexamples may imply the same 1/L threshold by effective-resistance scaling; full field not exhaustively indexed.
